children: Copper hit a record high on Tuesday as the market continued to focus on flows of the metal into the United States amid tightened supply elsewhere.
Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange
was up 0.6% at $14,597 a metric ton by 0330 GMT, after hitting a record $14,617 earlier in the session. It already set a record at $14,533 on Monday.
The most-traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange
climbed 1.36% to 110,690 yuan ($16,495.29) a ton, after rising as much as 1.54% to 110,890 yuan, its highest since January 30.
Copper continued to flow into U.S. warehouses, swelling COMEX inventories to a record 766,795 short tons, or 695,624 metric tons, as of last week.

“The still-elevated COMEX-LME price spread suggests physical copper continues to flow into the United States, deepening the supply tightness in markets outside the U.S.,” an analyst at Chinese broker Everbright Futures said.

Copper stocks in LME-registered warehouses saw more than 51% of their warrants cancelled. Inventories monitored by the SHFE (CU-SGH-STX) stood at around 63,000 tons last week, down 85% from a mid-March peak and the lowest since January 2024.
A premium of LME cash copper over the three-month contract (CMCU0-3), known as a backwardation, persisted, signalling tight near-term availability of the metal.

Elsewhere, the U.S. dollar hovered around recent lows, making metals denominated in the greenback cheaper for holders of other currencies, although expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates in September remained a headwind for risk assets.
Zinc also rallied, with three-month LME zinc
up 1.02% at $4,024 a ton by 0330 GMT, after touching $4,032, its highest in more than four years. And the most-traded SHFE zinc contract
jumped 2.37% to 27,635 yuan a ton, after touching 27,715 yuan, its highest since January 30.
Among other LME metals, aluminium
rose 0.23%, lead
was flat, nickel
added 0.12% and tin
fell 0.26%.
On the SHFE, aluminium
rose 0.51%, zinc
jumped 2.37%, lead
fell 0.68%, nickel
slipped 0.55% and tin
rose 0.46%.
($1 = 6.7104 Chinese yuan renminbi)
